messages.subject: uisng data.frame inside simmer
parts:
Hi,

I am looking for ways to make my code faster (currently it takes 1 hour to run 10,000 arrivals)
I was using add.generator and now I am trying the following:

Use add.dataframe for creating arrivals so now I need to know if I can keep using data.frame instructions inside simmer?

People$age <- ifelse(People$age_group == 1,sample(18:34,10000, replace = TRUE),ifelse(People$age_group == 2,sample(35:64,10000, replace = TRUE),sample(65:99,10000, replace = TRUE)))

This would help me change attributes of all 10,000 People at the same time instead of one by one as I currently have it using set_attribute.

Thanks,

Pablo.

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] uisng data.frame inside simmer
parts:
On Mon, 7 Oct 2019 at 23:10, Pablo Anaya <pablo...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> I am looking for ways to make my code faster (currently it takes 1 hour to run 10,000 arrivals)
> I was using add.generator and now I am trying the following:
>
> Use add.dataframe for creating arrivals so now I need to know if I can keep using data.frame instructions inside simmer?
>
> People$age <- ifelse(People$age_group == 1,sample(18:34,10000, replace = TRUE),ifelse(People$age_group == 2,sample(35:64,10000, replace = TRUE),sample(65:99,10000, replace = TRUE)))
>
> This would help me change attributes of all 10,000 People at the same time instead of one by one as I currently have it using set_attribute.

No, that's not how it works. The add_dataframe function makes it easy
(and fast) to feed a pre-computed set of arrivals with attributes, but
during the simulation, each line in the data frame still is a separate
arrival, and the same semantics apply.

If you want to speed up, you should first debug where's the
bottleneck. I suggest to use the profiler.

Iñaki
